system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

The computation of the rebates received by Licensee shall be expressed as a fixed percentage (15%) of Billable Platform Fees paid by Licensee to Licensor. The rebates shall be payable in shares of Licensor's Common Stock; priced at $.25 cents per share. The amount of rebates earned by Licensee shall be calculated for each tranche of 30 Billion of Notional Volume traded in the EPath FX Platform by Licensee. The amount of shares earned by Licensee shall terminate at the earlier of, the expiration of the term of this Agreement or the receipt of Six (6,000,000) Million shares of Licensor's common stock by Licensee. input.quote: The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly. In no event shall the amount payable by the Licensor be less than the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded with the Licensed Technology multiplied by the applicable Fees set forth above.
input.rationale: The pricing architecture is purely usage-based and imposes no minimum purchase, minimum volume, or take-or-pay obligation on us, so it meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only). Article V fixes "user fees" by reference to "Monthly Notional Volume bands (US$bn) traded on Platform by Licensee" at a per-US$1 million rate, and the monthly calculation in Article V.III(b) is driven by volume actually traded, with the only floor being actual recorded usage multiplied by the applicable rate — not a committed minimum. The volume bands are descending-rate tiers, not volume caps or thresholds we must reach, and Article V.i(ii) confirms the highest band reached simply lowers the rate for all trades that month. The other charges are for ordered services or one-off consideration: the $2,500 per month Technical Support Services fee under Article VII(a) (with Article VII(d) confirming "there shall be no additional fees payable by the Licensee to the Licensor for technical support services"), the Initial Payment, and the Supplemental Payments revenue share, which is a percentage of amounts we actually earn from third parties. Nothing in the document uses "minimum", "shortfall", "take or pay" or equivalent language, so the fallback (12-month cap, 30-day reduction, true-up) is not engaged and no redline is warranted. Two non-material observations for the file, noted rather than flagged: the apparent scrivener's error in Article V.III(b) referring to the amount payable "by the Licensor" where the payer is plainly the Licensee, and the 36-month initial term combined with the fixed monthly support fee — neither creates a volume commitment, though we may wish to correct the typo in any amendment.

- **Investigation:** Article XXI (Effect of Termination, p0138) is one-directional — our licences end and we must ship back all Licensed Technology, API Documentation and Confidential Information within 5 days with an officer's certificate. Article XX (change-of-control termination), Article XXIII, and General Provisions (p0144–p0160) contain no exit, migration, data-return, export or deletion mechanics; searches for transition/assistance/data return returned nothing responsive. - **Direction check:** the existing return obligation benefits Licensor, so it was not flagged; the gap is the absence of any reciprocal obligation on Licensor for a hosted platform holding our data.
- **Cure:** a single `insert_after` p0138 adding one short article carrying exactly the three fallback elements — assistance triggered on expiry or termination, at least 90 days of it, and export of our data within 30 days. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):

  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

Finding rationale:
The Agreement has no post-termination transition or data-return provision anywhere. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs one way only: licences terminate and Licensee must ship back Licensor's Licensed Technology and Confidential Information with an officer's certificate; nothing requires Licensor to help us migrate or to give back our own trading/market data held on its hosted platform. General Provisions and Article XX contain no exit mechanics either. Because this is a hosted FX platform where Licensor holds our data, the omission fails the fallback and approaches walk-away territory (no data return). We have inserted the fallback position only: at least 90 days of transition assistance and export of our data within 30 days of expiry or termination. We did not add the preferred six-month/then-current-rates and certified-deletion mechanics, which remain available if Licensor prefers that structure.

**Finding: MINCOMMIT — Compliant (meets the preferred position).**

- **Fees are usage-only.** Article V.II/V.III set "user fees" by reference to "Monthly Notional Volume bands (US$bn) traded on Platform by Licensee" at a per-US$1 million-traded rate, and the monthly amount is calculated on volume actually traded. The only floor is actual recorded usage × the applicable rate — not a committed minimum.
- **No minimum, shortfall, or take-or-pay.** Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay", "quota", "threshold", "whether or not used" and "guarantee" return nothing operative against us. The descending-rate tiers are pricing bands, not volume caps or targets we must hit (Article V.i(ii) only lowers the rate once a band is reached).
- **Other charges are ordered services or one-off consideration.** The $2,500/month Technical Support Services fee (Article VII(a), with VII(d) confirming no additional support fees), the $35,000 Initial Payment, and the 33% Supplemental Payments revenue share (payable only out of amounts we actually earn from third parties) are all payments for services ordered or usage, not volume commitments.
- **Fallback not engaged**, so no redline was proposed. Noted for the file only (not deviations): the scrivener's error in Article V.III(b) ("payable by the Licensor" where the payer is plainly the Licensee), and the 36-month term with fixed monthly support fee — neither creates a purchase or volume commitment.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Document: ARTICLE I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Agreement:

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-52117ca5","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"The only indemnity in the Agreement runs one way: Article XII (p0128-p0129) requires Licensee to defend and indemnify Licensor for the exercise of its own licence rights, its business conduct and any breach, and there is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the document (searches for \"indemn\", \"harmless\" and \"defend\" return no Licensor-side obligation). Article XIII compounds this by expressly providing that \"UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY HAS RESULTED ... IN ANY INFRINGEMENT ... OF THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ... RIGHTS OF ANY PERSON\", and caps all Licensor liability at one half of amounts paid. That is walk-away territory (no Vendor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity), so it fails the fallback. We propose the fallback package only: a Licensor IP indemnity with the customary Licensee modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap, plus two surgical \"subject to Article XIII-A\" conforming edits so the retained Article XIII infringement exclusion and 0.5x cap do not contradict the new indemnity. We have not sought the preferred additions (defence duty, affiliates, breach-of-law/data-breach/wilful-misconduct prongs, claim procedure, narrowed Licensee indemnity) at this level.","proposal":"Add Licensor IP indemnity with customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap, and conform the liability limits.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-b6210253","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, and does so at one half of all amounts we have paid — well below 6 months' fees on any reading — while our liability is left entirely uncapped (and is expanded by the one-way indemnity in Article XII and the exculpations in Article II). That is walk-away territory on two counts (one-sided cap; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees), so it fails the fallback. We have taken the fallback: the cap in (b) is now mutual and set at fees paid by Licensee in the 12 months preceding the claim, with a new (d) placing indemnification, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap. We have not pushed to the preferred position here (USD 1,000,000 floor, \"paid or payable\", mutual consequential-damages exclusion in (a), and data protection/fraud/IP carve-outs), which remains available if Licensor prefers to trade.","proposal":"Make the Article XIII cap mutual and set it at 12 months' fees, and place indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-d6b135ce","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Article XXIV(c) bars any Licensee assignment without Licensor consent with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, and imposes no restriction at all on Licensor assignment, so it fails even the fallback (no mutual successor right, no notice mechanic, no reasonableness standard). Article XX(a) compounds this by automatically terminating the Agreement and all of our licences on our Change of Control unless Licensor consents, with Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing on competitive or subjective \"adversely effected\" grounds — squarely walk-away territory. We therefore move to the preferred position: consent-free Licensee assignment to an Affiliate (defined in §1.1) or M&A successor, consent (not unreasonably withheld) for Licensor assignments with no assignment to our competitors, and no Licensor termination right on our change of control. The deleted change-of-control carve-out in §XXIV(c) also cross-referenced a non-existent \"Section 13.4(a)\"; the CHANGE OF CONTROL definition is retained. The Article XXII right of first refusal on a sale/merger is a separate commercial term and is not flagged here.","proposal":"Allow Licensee assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent, restrict Licensor assignment, and remove automatic termination on Licensee change of control.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-09da45b2","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, so it meets the preferred position. The licence is repeatedly and expressly \"Non Exclusive\" (preamble, Art. II §iii at p0030, Art. IV at p0049, Art. V at p0050), and nothing requires us to source Spot FX connectivity, liquidity or platform services solely from Licensor, to route all trading volume through the Platform, or to refrain from using competing platforms or providers. The volume-band fee table and rebate mechanics (p0056-p0076) price actual usage but set no minimum-volume or requirements commitment. The planner-flagged \"Right of First Refusal\" (Art. XXII, p0139) and the Change of Control consent right (Art. XX, p0134) are corporate-transaction controls, not sourcing restraints, and are properly assessed under ASSIGN/change-of-control rather than EXCLUSIVITY. The \"exclusive purpose\" wording in the Field of Use definition (p0007) is a field-of-use limit on how we may use Licensor's own Licensed Technology, not a restriction on buying from other suppliers; likewise the distribution/sublicensing restrictions at p0027, p0042 and p0085 govern onward transfer of Licensor's technology only. No fallback analysis is needed, and no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-8ca0d1c5","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The only ownership provision (Article III) is entirely Licensor-side: Licensor owns the Licensed Technology and all IP therein, and \"Derivative Work\" is defined to capture \"any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based upon or incorporating the Licensed Technology\". The customization work and unique client front end that we pay for under Article VII(b) therefore vest in Licensor with no ownership, assignment or lasting licence back to us; our only rights are a non-exclusive, Field-of-Use licence that Article XXI extinguishes on termination, and Article II bars us from modifying or sublicensing. There is also no statement of our rights in our own trading/transaction data. That fails every deliverables-licence element of the fallback, so we take the fallback rather than preferred: Licensor keeps ownership of its platform and know-how (already met by Article III), and we add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables for our business, plus a limit confining any Licensor right in our data to processing it solely to provide the services. Article XXI is conformed so the Deliverables licence is not automatically terminated.","proposal":"Add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense customization deliverables, limit Licensor's rights in our data, and conform the termination clause.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-e485e6ce","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee, or minimum-fee-on-termination payable by Licensee, so the preferred position (\"Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties\") is met. I checked the fee and payment articles (Article V user fees, Article VII support fee of $2,500/month, Supplemental Payments, tax gross-up), the term and termination provisions (Articles IV, XIX–XXI) and the remedies provisions (Articles XI, XIII, XXIII). Licensee's monetary obligations are all usage- or service-based consideration: on Licensor's termination for breach, Licensor retains only \"the right to receive payments for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology\" (p0049) — actual accrued fees, not a stipulated sum or acceleration of remaining contract value. Article XXIII (p0142) affirmatively bars termination-related damages of any kind against either party. Two provisions are cost-shifting rather than liquidated damages and are not flagged: Licensee bears audit cost if a discrepancy over 5% is found (p0064), and Licensee pays standard rates for out-of-scope error work (p0095). The rebate mechanic in p0076 runs in our favour. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-55014129","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The grant in Article II.iii runs to Licensee alone, and the \"notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary\" restrictions bar any use or access by third parties (p0041) or by \"any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee\" (p0045), so Affiliates are excluded with no path to add them. On transfer, Article XX(a) provides that the licence \"shall automatically terminate\" on a Change of Control (asset sale, merger or control transfer) absent Licensor's prior written consent, which Licensor may withhold on broad grounds, and the assignment clause routes all M&A to that section. The clause therefore fails both fallback elements. We have targeted the fallback: Affiliates covered on written notice (with the two conflicting use restrictions conformed) and continuation/transfer to a successor in an M&A. We have not pursued the preferred items (contractor coverage, perpetual/irrevocable paid-up rights, termination only for uncured material breach under the 36-month term in Article IV).","proposal":"Extend licence to Licensee's Affiliates on written notice and allow the licence to continue/transfer to a successor on a Change of Control instead of terminating.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-44cfe916","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Agreement:","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restraint on our business, so it meets the preferred position. The only \"Field of Use\" language (p0007, applied by the grant in p0030) limits how we may use Licensor's own Licensed Technology; it does not restrict the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, and Licensor's licence is expressly non-exclusive with Licensor free to license others (p0043). Every other restriction in Article II (no distribution, no Derivative Works, no reverse engineering) is tied to the Licensed Technology itself rather than to our operations, and nothing prevents us from developing, acquiring or licensing competing FX platforms. The sole post-term covenant binding us is the three-year employee non-solicit (p0125), which falls under the non-solicitation rule, and the change-of-control consent/right of first refusal are assignment-and-exit mechanics reviewed under the assignment rules; neither is a restraint on competing activity, so we do not flag them here. Worth noting commercially, but not a playbook deviation: the Field of Use is confined to Spot FX, so extending it to other FX products would require Licensor's agreement.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-bbbb9c84","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The Agreement commits Licensee to a 36-month Initial Period (extendable/renewable) but nowhere gives Licensee any right to terminate for convenience: Licensor's termination rights (Articles IV, XIX, XX) are all for breach, insolvency or change of control, and Licensee has no notice-based exit and no refund of prepaid fees. Absence of a Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months fails both the preferred and fallback positions, so we insert a 30-day convenience termination right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Licensor is not given any convenience right today; we state that expressly so the position cannot be read into the renewal mechanics.","proposal":"Add Licensee convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and bar Licensor convenience termination during the term.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-052b44a8","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"50+ US$5.00","rationale":"Article IV(b) is the only audit right binding us, with the cost allocation sitting separately in p0064. Two good features are already present: the auditor must be an independent CPA or Audit Professional selected by mutual agreement, and Licensor bears audit cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found (the preferred cost threshold). However, the clause imposes no frequency limit (Licensor may request audits repeatedly) and gives no advance notice period — the \"within 30 days of receipt of a written request\" language is a deadline for us to submit to the audit, not notice to us. It therefore fails the fallback on frequency and notice, approaching the unlimited-audit walk-away, and is also silent on business hours, auditor confidentiality, off-site conduct and system access. We have made the shortest edit to the preferred level, leaving the independent-auditor and 5% cost terms untouched.","proposal":"Add frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality, off-site and no-system-access limits to the Licensor audit right","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-8b204527","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"The only governing-law/venue provision is General Provisions (a) (p0145-p0146): the Agreement is governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, and all suits must be instituted in the City of New York with irrevocable submission to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Southern District of New York or any New York State court, plus a venue and forum non conveniens waiver. There is no arbitration provision (no responsive text for \"arbitration\"), no foreign seat, and no competing forum elsewhere in the document. This sits at our preferred position: New York law with exclusive state and federal court jurisdiction in New York. Two immaterial points noted only: the venue is expressed as the \"City of New York\" rather than New York County (which encompasses Manhattan/New York County and includes the S.D.N.Y. and New York State courts sitting there), and the clause contains no express carve-out for temporary injunctive relief elsewhere — the absence of that carve-out makes exclusivity stronger for us, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-63c9f66f","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"Pricing is set by the per-ticket volume tiers (p0056-p0067) and Supplemental Payments (p0078) with no best-terms undertaking, and there is no MFN in either direction on fees. However, Article XXII imposes a right-to-match / most-favoured-offer mechanic on us: we must disclose any bonafide third-party offer for our assets or a merger and give the Licensor a first-refusal window before we may proceed (p0139-p0141). Under the playbook that disclosure/right-to-match mechanic is an MFN-type obligation burdening the Customer, and it fails every fallback element: it is not limited to a defined product, it runs for the whole term (36 months, extendable seven years at the Licensor's option per p0049) rather than 12 months, and it has no like-for-like comparison carve-outs. We therefore take the preferred position and remove the obligation, keeping our right to consummate the third-party transaction. The related Change of Control consent right (p0134) is a separate mechanic and is not flagged here.","proposal":"Remove the Licensor's right of first refusal / right to match third-party offers to Licensee","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-0e02915f","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The pricing architecture is purely usage-based and imposes no minimum purchase, minimum volume, or take-or-pay obligation on us, so it meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only). Article V fixes \"user fees\" by reference to \"Monthly Notional Volume bands (US$bn) traded on Platform by Licensee\" at a per-US$1 million rate, and the monthly calculation in Article V.III(b) is driven by volume actually traded, with the only floor being actual recorded usage multiplied by the applicable rate — not a committed minimum. The volume bands are descending-rate tiers, not volume caps or thresholds we must reach, and Article V.i(ii) confirms the highest band reached simply lowers the rate for all trades that month. The other charges are for ordered services or one-off consideration: the $2,500 per month Technical Support Services fee under Article VII(a) (with Article VII(d) confirming \"there shall be no additional fees payable by the Licensee to the Licensor for technical support services\"), the Initial Payment, and the Supplemental Payments revenue share, which is a percentage of amounts we actually earn from third parties. Nothing in the document uses \"minimum\", \"shortfall\", \"take or pay\" or equivalent language, so the fallback (12-month cap, 30-day reduction, true-up) is not engaged and no redline is warranted. Two non-material observations for the file, noted rather than flagged: the apparent scrivener's error in Article V.III(b) referring to the amount payable \"by the Licensor\" where the payer is plainly the Licensee, and the 36-month initial term combined with the fixed monthly support fee — neither creates a volume commitment, though we may wish to correct the typo in any amendment.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-ab0d318a","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"Article X(b) binds only the Licensee (us), reaches every person employed by Licensor and its Affiliates rather than personnel directly involved in the services, and runs for the Term plus three years after expiration or termination. That exceeds the 24-month/all-personnel walk-away threshold and fails the fallback on mutuality, scope and duration. The paragraph's definition of \"Solicit\" already delivers the general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and there is no no-hire prohibition (only solicitation \"to leave\" employment). We have therefore replaced the first sentence with a mutual restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services provided under this Agreement and running for a single period of twelve (12) months after that person's involvement ends, deleting the standing \"Term of this Agreement\" limb so nothing can extend the covenant beyond that cap; the carve-out sentence is left verbatim. The result sits at the accepted fallback, not the preferred no-non-solicit position.","proposal":"Make the non-solicit mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, and running only twelve (12) months after that involvement ends.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-renewal-06d830b8","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"Article IV (p0049) is the only renewal provision in the Agreement. It lets Licensor unilaterally extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years at its sole option, with no Licensee consent, no non-renewal notice window and no cap on renewal length. That is a multi-year renewal imposed on us and sits in walk-away territory, well below the fallback (non-renewal window of no more than 60 days). It also contradicts the same Article's sentences II and III, which contemplate extension only \"by mutual written of the parties\" / \"by mutual agreement in writing\". We therefore delete the unilateral option and make renewal mutual-written-agreement only, which satisfies the preferred position; the remaining preferred elements (12-month renewal term, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) and the price-uplift cap are conditional on automatic renewal and renewal price increases, neither of which exists once the Licensor option is removed (the user-fee schedule in Article V sets fees for the Initial Period with no renewal uplift mechanic).","proposal":"Renewal only by mutual written agreement; remove Licensor's unilateral 7-year extension option.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-9eb7c916","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"The Agreement has no post-termination transition or data-return provision anywhere. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs one way only: licences terminate and Licensee must ship back Licensor's Licensed Technology and Confidential Information with an officer's certificate; nothing requires Licensor to help us migrate or to give back our own trading/market data held on its hosted platform. General Provisions and Article XX contain no exit mechanics either. Because this is a hosted FX platform where Licensor holds our data, the omission fails the fallback and approaches walk-away territory (no data return). We have inserted the fallback position only: at least 90 days of transition assistance and export of our data within 30 days of expiry or termination. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — E-Path FX Platform Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-House Counsel (Customer/Licensee side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Licensor's draft — verified findings

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the draft Licence Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, six clauses are compliant and require no redline, nine are deviations requiring negotiation, and three rules are unaddressed in the document altogether.

The risk in this draft is concentrated in the allocation of liability and in our ability to exit. Two findings are critical. First, the only indemnity in the Agreement runs against us: Article XII requires Licensee to defend and indemnify Licensor, and there is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the document, while Article XIII expressly excludes Licensor liability for infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology. Second, Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, at one half of amounts we have paid, while leaving our own liability uncapped. Each of these sits in walk-away territory on our playbook, and they compound one another.

The exit and control provisions are the next priority. We are committed to a 36-month Initial Period with no convenience termination right, Licensor may unilaterally extend that term by a further seven years at its sole option under Article IV, our licence automatically terminates on a Change of Control under Article XX(a), and Article XXII obliges us to disclose and offer Licensor a right to match any third-party offer for our assets or a merger. There is also no post-termination transition or data-return obligation on Licensor, notwithstanding that this is a hosted platform holding our trading data.

On the positive side, several commercially significant terms are already acceptable: the licence is expressly non-exclusive with no sourcing or non-compete restraint on us, pricing is purely usage-based with no minimum commitment or take-or-pay, there are no liquidated damages or early-termination fees payable by us, and governing law and venue sit at our preferred position (New York law, exclusive New York state and federal jurisdiction, no arbitration).

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. XII, p0128–p0129; Art. XIII) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions (Art. XXIV(c); Art. XX(a)) |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. III; Art. VII(b); Art. XXI) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. II.iii, p0041, p0045; Art. XX(a)) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Arts. IV, XIX, XX) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § I Certain Definitions |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Deviation | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. XXII, p0139–p0141) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. IV, p0049) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX; p0093) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Art. IV(b); p0064 |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | Confidential Information/Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b), p0125) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (a), p0145–p0146 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. V; Art. VII) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | General Provisions (p0144–p0159) |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following provisions fall into walk-away territory under our playbook and must move before we can sign:

1. **No Licensor indemnity, coupled with a one-way Licensee indemnity (Art. XII / Art. XIII).** We carry the defence and indemnity obligation for the exercise of our own licence rights, while Article XIII expressly provides that Licensor shall not be liable for infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology. Our fallback ask is a Licensor IP indemnity with the customary modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap, plus conforming "subject to Article XIII-A" edits so the retained exclusion and cap do not contradict the new indemnity.

2. **One-sided liability cap set below six months' fees (Art. XIII).** The cap applies only to Licensor and is set at one half of amounts paid, with our liability uncapped and expanded by Article XII and the Article II exculpations. Fallback: a mutual cap at fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim, with indemnification, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap.

3. **Automatic termination of the licence on our Change of Control (Art. XX(a)), with no assignment carve-outs (Art. XXIV(c)).** Licensor may refuse consent on competitive or subjective "adversely effected" grounds, and there is no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no restriction on Licensor assignment. We seek the preferred position: consent-free assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor, consent (not unreasonably withheld) for Licensor assignments with no assignment to our competitors, and removal of the Licensor termination right on our change of control.

4. **Licensor's unilateral seven-year extension option (Art. IV, p0049).** Licensor may extend the 36-month Initial Period at its sole option with no Licensee consent and no non-renewal window — and this contradicts the same Article's own "mutual agreement in writing" language. We require renewal by mutual written agreement only.

5. **"AS IS" supply with no performance warranty (Art. VIX).** All warranties are disclaimed and Licensor expressly does not warrant that errors or nonconformity to the Documentation will be corrected; the commercially-reasonable-efforts Error Correction covenant at p0093 is not a substitute. Fallback: 90-day Software conformance warranty, 30-day services warranty, repair/replace/refund, with carve-outs from the disclaimer.

6. **No data return or transition assistance (Art. XXI).** Article XXI runs one way — our licences terminate and we return Licensor's property — with no obligation on Licensor to return our trading and market data held on its hosted platform. Fallback: at least 90 days' transition assistance and export of our data within 30 days of expiry or termination.

We also note two items that approach walk-away territory: the unlimited-frequency, no-notice audit right in Article IV(b), and the absence of any insurance covenant given that Licensor routes our market data and Spot FX trading activity through its platform.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Proposals are drafted and verified for all nine deviations and the three missing-clause insertions. The NOSOLICIT edit was repaired during verification and should be re-read before the draft goes out.
2. **Lead with the liability package.** Present INDEMN and LOL-CAP together as a single trade: a Licensor IP indemnity at a 3x annual fees super-cap in exchange for a mutual 12-month cap with the standard carve-outs. We have deliberately held back the preferred asks (USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", mutual consequential-damages exclusion, data protection/fraud/IP carve-outs, defence duty, affiliates and claim procedure) as trading room.
3. **Treat the exit cluster as one negotiation.** ASSIGN, LICENSE (Art. XX(a) automatic termination), T4C, RENEWAL, MFN (Art. XXII right of first refusal) and TRANSITION all bear on our ability to leave or to be acquired. Sequencing them together avoids conceding one and being met with another.
4. **Confirm the commercial position on deliverables.** The customization work and unique client front end we pay for under Article VII(b) currently vest in Licensor via the "Derivative Work" definition. Please confirm with the business how material those deliverables are, so we can calibrate between the fallback licence-back and a fuller ownership ask.
5. **Housekeeping to raise in any amendment.** Two non-material drafting points for the file: the Article V.III(b) reference to amounts payable "by the Licensor" where the payer is plainly the Licensee, and the now-deleted §XXIV(c) cross-reference to a non-existent "Section 13.4(a)".
6. **Flag for business, not legal.** The Field of Use is confined to Spot FX; extending it to other FX products would require Licensor's agreement. This is a commercial scoping question rather than a playbook deviation."}
